title: Hold Length and Referral Window Limits for the Ostomy Supply Program
content:
Three program-status limits of the Ostomy Supply Program are set per payer tier: whether shipments must be held during an inpatient stay, the longest time a program may stay on hold, and the time allowed to complete referral documentation.

- **Inpatient hold required** - whether shipments must be held while the customer is an inpatient in a hospital or skilled nursing facility, because the payer does not pay home supplies during a covered stay.
- **Longest hold** - the longest time a program may remain on hold, in calendar days counted from the hold start date, before it is closed administratively.
- **Referral documentation window** - the time allowed to complete the referral documentation (written order on file and, where required, the prior authorization decided), in calendar days counted from the program's enrolled date.

| Tier | Inpatient hold required | Longest hold | Referral documentation window |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ostomy Self-Pay Program | No | 180 days | 30 days |
| Ostomy Commercial HMO Program | Yes | 60 days | 30 days |
| Ostomy Commercial PPO Program | Yes | 90 days | 30 days |
| Ostomy Medicare Advantage Program | Yes | 90 days | 30 days |
| Ostomy Original Medicare Program | Yes | 90 days | 30 days |
| Ostomy Medicaid Program | Yes | 60 days | 30 days |

**Reading the table.** Every insured tier holds shipments during an inpatient stay; the Ostomy Self-Pay Program does not. The longest hold is 60 days on the Commercial HMO and Medicaid tiers, 90 days on the Commercial PPO, Medicare Advantage and Original Medicare tiers, and 180 days on the self-pay tier. The referral documentation window is 30 days on every tier.
